//: Enforces the design system's core invariant: component CSS consumes tokens through the SEMANTIC layer only — never a raw hex / named / rgb-hsl colour, and never ANY primitive variable (var(--primitive-…), colour OR size). The semantic layer is what makes brand-switching and density-switching work at the component level. Scoped to component module CSS via the lint script. Sebell runs a true density setup: every spacing value scales via semantic tokens, with no fixed-primitive exceptions.
//2: The value rule also bans raw px/rem/em on the properties where the semantic layer is TOTAL — spacing (padding / margin / gap), radius, and font-size. Those are decisions, and every one of them has a token. It is deliberately NOT extended to border-width, box-shadow geometry or gradient stops: the system has no token for those (the only width token is --components-focus-ring-width), so a ban there would push you into binding a token that merely equals the value today. That is the Switch-height mistake documented in CLAUDE.md. If those need tokens, add them in Figma first, then tighten this rule.

declaration-property-value-disallowed-li.message: Component CSS must go through the semantic token layer: no var(--primitive-…), and no raw px/rem/em for spacing, radius or font-size. Use the matching semantic token — --semantic-components-* for spacing INSIDE one object, --semantic-layout-* for spacing BETWEEN objects, --radius-* for corners, --typography-font-size-* for type. If no token fits, that is a Figma question — ask before hardcoding.
